Cropped native-pixel at the cheek/eye, the nose/mouth and the hand: pore texture is natural, no whorl, lashes resolve individually, four fingers with correct nail beds and cuticles. Clean.

NO PRODUCT IN FRAME, so no label to misspell and no brand mark to draw wrong — the two failure modes that dominate this store's image QA do not apply.

WHY THIS PICTURE SUITS THIS BLOCK. The copy is the problem statement: the renewal cycle slows with age, and the result is 'a duller complexion, accumulated signs of environmental stress and a loss of the glow'. The frame is a woman with visible uneven tone and sun spots on the cheek, eyes closed, the back of her fingers resting against her jaw — the condition the block describes, before any product is named. Note this is NOT the register the batch was briefed for (it was generated for the copper-peptide f3 satisfaction block, which wanted a pleased, unblemished face); repurposed here deliberately, and it reads better as a cause than as a result.

OPTIMISATION, PER THE MEASURED RULE. Do not read the 714K JPEG as a regression. Shopify's CDN transcodes to WebP and resizes per srcset, so this source is never what a visitor downloads; re-encoding it smaller first hands the WebP encoder JPEG artefacts and costs delivered bytes (measured 2026-08-24: a 41% smaller source delivered MORE bytes at every width). So: q95, 4:4:4, progressive, metadata dropped, and the long edge left at 2048. This block's sizes attribute is `(max-width: 999px) 100vw, min(720px, 50vw)`, so the widest it is ever asked for is 2x on a 999px viewport = 1998px — 2048 covers retina exactly with nothing dead. Delivered bytes verified off the live CDN after publish, never the local file size.
